message.content:
The Declaration of Independence was signed by **56 delegates** from the thirteen colonies who represented the Continental Congress. Some of the most well‑known signers include:

| Signer | State / Colony | Notable Contributions |
|--------|----------------|-----------------------|
| **John Hancock** | Massachusetts | His bold signature became a symbol of American patriotism; he served as President of the Second Continental Congress. |
| **Thomas Jefferson** | Virginia | Principal author of the Declaration; later became the third U.S. President. |
| **Benjamin Franklin** | Pennsylvania | Renowned statesman and scientist; helped secure French support during the Revolution. |
| **George Washington** | Virginia | Commander-in-Chief of the Continental Army; later the first U.S. President. |
| **Samuel Adams** | Massachusetts | Key organizer of the Boston Tea Party and early advocate for independence. |
| **John Adams** | Massachusetts | Future second U.S. President; influential diplomat in France. |
| **James Madison** | Virginia | Later known as the “Father of the Constitution.” |
| **Alexander Hamilton** | New York | Founding father and first Secretary of Treasury. |
| **John Jay** | New York | Diplomat and co-author of the Federalist Papers. |
| **Robert Morris** | Pennsylvania | Financier of the Revolutionary War; later a signer of the Constitution. |

Other notable signers include **Patrick Henry**, **Paul Revere**, **John Witherspoon**, **William Floyd**, **Francis Lewis**, **Lewis Morris**, **Richard Henry Lee**, **Charles Carroll of Carrollton** (the only Catholic signer), and many others.

These individuals signed the document on **July 4, 1776** (though the formal signing ceremony actually took place on August 2, 1776). Their signatures were affixed to the original parchment in the presence of the Continental Congress, marking a pivotal moment in American history.
